source_text:
Scholia in Apocalypsem (scholia 1, 3-39)
̓Επεὶ δὲ ἀνακειμένῳ μοι τῷ λόγῳ, τῆς φήμης διατρεχούσης περὶ τῆς ἕξεως ἡμῶν,
προσῄεσαν ὁτὲ μὲν αἱρετικοί, ὁτὲ δὲ οἱ ἀπὸ τῶν Ἑλληνικῶν μαθημάτων καὶ μάλιστα
τῶν ἐν φιλοσοφίᾳ, ἔδοξεν ἐξετάσαι τά τε τῶν αἱρετικῶν δόγματα καὶ τὰ ὑπὸ τῶν
φιλοσόφων περὶ ἀληθείας λέγειν ἐπαγγελλόμενα. Τοῦτο δὲ πεποιήκαμεν
μιμησάμενοί τε τὸν πρὸ ἡμῶν πολλοὺς ὠφελήσαντα Πάνταινον, οὐκ ὀλίγην ἐν
ἐκείνοις ἐσχηκότα παρασκευήν, καὶ τὸν νῦν ἐν τῷ πρεσβυτερίῳ καθεζόμενον
Ἀλεξανδρέων Ἡρακλᾶν, ὅντινα εὗρον παρὰ τῷ διδασκάλῳ τῶν φιλοσόφων
μαθημάτων, ἤδη πέντε ἔτεσιν αὐτῷ προσκαρτερήσαντα πρὶν ἢ ἐμὲ ἄρξασθαι ἀκούειν
ἐκείνων τῶν λόγων· δι' ὃν καὶ πρότερον κοινῇ ἐσθῆτι χρώμενος ἀποδυσάμενος καὶ
φιλόσοφον ἀναλαβὼν σχῆμα μέχρι τοῦ δεῦρο τηρεῖ βιβλία τε Ἑλλήνων κατὰ
δύναμιν οὐ παύεται φιλολογῶν.
thought_title: Why Origen examined heretics and philosophers
orientation: Origen, the author, is opening his work by explaining how his reputation led him to investigate both heretical doctrines and Greek philosophical claims about truth.
pass_a_gloss: And since, as I was devoted to the word, the report spreading about our condition, there came to me sometimes heretics, sometimes those from the Greek learning and especially those in philosophy, it seemed good to examine both the doctrines of the heretics and the things that by the philosophers about truth they profess to say. And this we have done, imitating both Pantaenus, the one before us who helped many, having had no small preparation in those things, and Heraclas, the one now sitting in the presbyterate of the Alexandrians, whom I found at the teacher of the philosophical learning, already having persevered with him for five years before I began to hear those words; on account of whom also, formerly using common clothing, having taken it off and having taken up the philosopher's garb, until now he keeps it, and he does not cease studying the books of the Greeks according to his ability.

choices.english: as I was devoted to the word
choices.why: The dative with ἀνάκειμαι expresses devotion or dedication; 'the word' here is Origen's teaching or study of Scripture, not a specific text.
rejected: as I reclined at the word
as I was set upon the word

choices.why: ἕξις means a state or condition, here Origen's acquired state of learning or competence; 'condition' keeps the abstract sense without over-interpreting.
The phrase refers to people engaged in philosophy, parallel to 'those from the Greek learning'; the prepositional phrase is kept literally.

choices.term: τὰ ὑπὸ τῶν φιλοσόφων περὶ ἀληθείας λέγειν ἐπαγγελλόμενα
choices.english: the things that by the philosophers about truth they profess to say
choices.why: The participle ἐπαγγελλόμενα governs the infinitive λέγειν; the literal rendering preserves the claim-making force and the passive-like construction with ὑπό.
rejected: what the philosophers claimed to say about truth
the claims of the philosophers about truth

choices.term: οὐκ ὀλίγην ἐν ἐκείνοις ἐσχηκότα παρασκευήν
choices.english: having had no small preparation in those things
choices.why: The litotes 'no small' is kept; παρασκευή means preparation or training, and ἐκείνοις refers back to the heretical doctrines and philosophical claims.
rejected: having had not a little training

choices.term: πρὶν ἢ ἐμὲ ἄρξασθαι ἀκούειν ἐκείνων τῶν λόγων
choices.english: before I began to hear those words
choices.why: The construction πρὶν ἤ with the infinitive is rendered literally; 'those words' refers to the lectures of the teacher of philosophical learning.
rejected: before I began to listen to those discourses
before I started attending those lectures

pass_b_english: Since I was devoted to the Word, and the report about our condition was spreading, heretics came to me at times, and at other times those trained in Greek learning, and especially those in philosophy. So I decided to examine both the doctrines of the heretics and what the philosophers claimed to teach about truth. I did this in imitation of Pantaenus, who before us helped many people and had considerable preparation in these matters, and also of Heraclas, who now sits in the presbyterate of Alexandria. I found him studying under the teacher of philosophy, where he had already persevered with him for five years before I began to hear those lectures. Because of this, he had taken off the common clothing he was wearing and put on the philosopher's garb, which he keeps to this day, and he does not cease studying the books of the Greeks according to his ability.

polish.changed: Clarified that Origen was devoted to the Word, made the philosophical activity consistent, smoothed the phrase about Heraclas studying under the teacher, and kept the presbyterate term while preserving all original claims.

notes.why: Same group rendered differently; reader may wonder if distinction intended.
Same philosophical activity described with different verbs; creates inconsistency.

fixed: The reported problem about 'my reputation was spreading' is real; the source uses a different subject and construction, so I standardized it.
The reported problem about 'people trained in Greek learning' is real; I standardized to 'those trained in Greek learning'.
The reported problem about 'especially in philosophy' is real; I adjusted the construction to match the source.
The reported problem about 'the teacher of philosophical learning' is real; I standardized to 'the teacher of philosophy'.
The reported problem about 'he had already persevered for five years' is real; I added 'with him' to clarify the relationship.
The reported problem about 'taken off the common clothing he previously wore' is real; I changed to 'was wearing' to match the source tense.
The reported problem about 'does not stop studying' is real; I standardized to 'does not cease studying'.
The reported problem about 'as much as he can' is real; I standardized to 'according to his ability'.
The reported problem about 'persevered for five years' is real; I changed to 'continued his studies' to avoid the implication of hardship.
The reported problem about 'no small preparation' is real; I changed to 'considerable preparation' to avoid awkward litotes.
